title: Breakwave Bi-Weekly Tanker Report - November 3, 2026
summary:
Main
• VLCC Remain Strong on Low Vessel Availability, Geopolitics - The recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports has yet to restore normal tanker circulation, with October flows through Hormuz averaging approximately 11.7 million barrels/day, up from 9.8 million barrels/day in September but below the pre-war level of 14.5 million barrels/day. Meanwhile, Middle Eastern VLCC tonne-miles remain 34% below 2025 levels and tonne-days 24% below pre-war levels, highlighting the disconnect between exceptionally high freight and underlying transportation demand . Around 80 VLCCs remain engaged in Gulf-of-Oman shuttle operations, with average round voyages extending to 23 days against an optimal 9-10 days, while offshore transfer bottlenecks and dedicated producer-controlled employment continue to constrain spot availability.
